summary: 完成经济学与机制设计领域输入：依据两篇已阅读的诺贝尔奖官方综述，整理了三种可迁移的形式结构和三个尚未解决的张力；未提出跨领域最终 idea，也未做实验。

structures.name: Strategic implementation under dispersed private information
structures.relation: Represent an institution as rules mapping participants' messages or actions to outcomes, and ask whether the desired allocation can arise when information is private and participants pursue their own interests. The key question shifts from 'what outcome is best?' to 'what rules make that outcome incentive-compatible and attainable?'
assumptions: Participants have preferences or objectives that can differ.
Some relevant information is privately held or dispersed.
The institution can be described by rules linking messages or actions to outcomes.

sources.title: Mechanism Design Theory: The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2007 (Press Release)
sources.content_note: Official review summary states that preferences and production information are dispersed, actors may use private information in their own interests, and mechanism design studies allocations accounting for incentives and private information.

structures.name: Stability as absence of mutually profitable deviations
structures.relation: For a matching, define an outcome as stable when there is no pair of participants who would both prefer to leave their current assignments for one another. This reframes quality around the set of feasible deviations and can be analyzed alongside efficiency and incentives to manipulate.
assumptions: There are two sides whose members can be paired or assigned.
Participants can rank or compare feasible partners.
A blocking pair is meaningful in the institution being modeled.

sources.title: Stable Allocations and the Practice of Market Design: The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2012 (Press Release)
sources.content_note: Official review defines stability through the absence of two agents who prefer each other over their current matches; it reports that Gale-Shapley methods guarantee stable matching and limit manipulation incentives.

structures.name: Institutional rules distribute both incentives and advantage
structures.relation: Treat a mechanism's procedural details as substantive: proposal order, permitted transfers, and which deviations count can affect strategic incentives and systematically advantage one side. Practical design therefore relates abstract properties to the actual constraints of an institution.
assumptions: The mechanism has design choices that alter feasible actions or outcomes.
The sides may have asymmetric roles or constraints.
Institution-specific restrictions, including ethical rules, can rule out otherwise feasible mechanisms.

sources.title: Stable Allocations and the Practice of Market Design: The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 2012 (Press Release)
sources.content_note: Official review notes that particular methods may systematically benefit one side and describes practical adaptations for local circumstances and ethical restrictions, including excluding side payments.

open_tensions: A mechanism may improve allocative efficiency while becoming harder to make truthful or strategy-resistant when participants hold private information; which incentive constraints are essential depends on what participants know and can report.

Stability prevents mutually beneficial blocking deviations, but it does not by itself select a distributionally fair or welfare-maximizing outcome; the definition of blocking and the choice of proposing side can change who benefits.

A formally attractive mechanism may rely on transfers or choices that an actual institution forbids for ethical or legal reasons; how should the design objective change when the feasible rule set is normatively restricted?

artifacts.kind: structured domain card; interpretations grounded in source notes
retrieval notes distinguishing source observations from interpretations

evidence.detail: 2007 Nobel Prize press release states that preferences and production information are dispersed, actors may use private information in their own interests, and mechanism design accounts for incentives and private information.

2012 Nobel Prize press release defines matching stability by the absence of a mutually preferred pair, reports that Gale-Shapley methods guarantee stable matching and limit manipulation, and notes side-specific advantages and ethical limits on transfers.
These passages support expressing design questions through implementability, feasible deviations, and institution-specific constraints; they do not establish novelty of these structures.

claims: The disciplinary card identifies three portable structures and three unresolved tensions relevant to economics and mechanism design.
Both cited sources were actually retrieved and read on 2026-11-04; they are official review summaries, not the underlying primary research papers.
limitations: Only two short official review sources were used; this is a bounded disciplinary input, not an exhaustive literature review.
The structures are established economics concepts and are not claimed as novel.
No cross-field idea generation, experiment, implementation, or novelty assessment was performed at this stage.
next_actions: Pass the card to the synthesis stage as disciplinary input, preserving its distinctions between source claims and interpretations.
Let the final checker separately assess similarity to existing work and obvious mathematical or logical errors for generated ideas.
